I had no idea when getting this game how engrossing it would be. The base game alone offers quite a bit of content and a solid gameplay experience that lasted me a good number of hours. But once you get into the mod workshop and community the game really opens up. It's such a good framework for crafting various stories and experiences, especially with mods, that no two playthroughs will ever feel quite the same. I highly recommend this game to those who like longer strategic and planning type games. It's not for everyone, gameplay can be slow and you can play for hours without anything particularly "exciting" happening, but that slow and steady progress towards longer term goals is very satisfying if that's your thing.
It took a few tries for it to click, but I just played all day today and I'm loving it.

Rimworld is not just a game, it's THE game. It's truly the pinncale of game development. The reason for that is that Rimworld can be played endlessly. There are so many different scenarios and unusual situations you can find yourself in that it never becomes boring. You can play as a tribe, trying to survive in lush jungles. Space pirates, raiding villages and enslaving everyone. A vampire cult, hiding in the furthest outskirts of the world and slowly growing in power. A secret order, trying to secure, contain and protect different anomalies to save the world and it's people. The possibilities are truly endless. You can play this game for hundreds of hours and it still will manage to surprise and entertain you. Buying Rimworld is possibly the best money to entertainment ratio you can find. And it supports an indie developer. So what are you waiting for?

I'll admit, when I first saw this game I didn't think it looked like much. I ended up ignoring it for other games for years. But I gotta say, damn this game is wild. I've always enjoyed my strategy games and this one scratches a weird itch I didn't know I had.

The game has the perfect balance of control/randomness. With a metric f*** ton of customization options for your colony/colonists, you can always style things the way you want them to be. Every play through will feel very different from the last, even if you try to play it the exact same way.

The mods are the biggest part for me! The modding community is always coming out with new content that feel like their own DLC at times. I recommend the vanilla expanded mod series for an extra boost of great content.

If you're in to sim/management games, this is very much worth a try.

Objectively the best game I've ever bought. It might be expensive with every DLC but, as many others have said, it's absolutely worth it. You're getting way more than you've paid for.

You want to play as goody-two-shoes ranchers? You can. Want to roleplay a cannibal, genetically and cybernetically augmented samurai dynasty? Go for it. Maybe you want to play as puritan slave runners? This game has got you covered.

You can engage with absolutely every element of the game (building a robot army, ranching, selling drugs, raiding, containing demons from outer dimension, cyborgs, gene-tailoring, warhammer psy magic, etc.) at the same time, or focus on something particular and build your colony around one-two aspects.

This game is truly endless. It took me over 1000 hours to beat it for the first time (don't look at my steam hours - I've played the game on GOG before buying a second copy on steam), and even then I only got one of 4 endings.

If you can't afford or don't want to buy all DLCs, at least buy Biotech, as it adds the most content.

Another huge perk of this game is its mod-friendliness. Now don't got downloading hundreds of mods right off the bat. Play at least two-three times before getting into modding.

So I like RimWorld. It's a genuinely fun game, and I've spent a while playing it. But there are other reviews that will tell you about how awesome this visually rendered user-friendly version of Dwarf Fortress is, so I'm going to talk about its problems instead.

The biggest issue with RimWorld as it currently exists is the storyteller system. The game is designed to continually push your base to its very last leg... and then leave it standing. You'll be raided by pirates who are happy to take only a couple of captives, natives who will lose 20 people in a raid and stop because they lit something on fire, and robots who will suddenly lose interest because you walked outside of their designated range. You'll be battered alive by animals who lose interest the moment a character is incapacitated, and hit by crop blights that time themselves to avoid actually starving our your colony.

So what gives?

RimWorld has the reputation of a game that you should lose. But I've still never taken a base to completion (victory or otherwise) because getting a slap on the wrist from murderous bloodthirsty pirates feels so... wrong. Disease will kill you, starvation will kill you, and hypo/hyperthermia will kill you... but you have to actively let those things happen.

RimWorld wants to tell you a story. I just wish I weren't the kind of protagonist that was unable to die no matter how badly he screwed up.

This game allows me to commit warcrimes and get away with it, similar to what Netanyahu does in Gaza.

This is a solid game, there is no way to deny this.
However, it does try to convey certain ideas that are immersion breaking for intelligent people.
- Inevitability: The Solar Flare event is a prime example of this. Not even late game tech can remedy it. This is unacceptable for someone who believes everything can be overcome if one puts his mind to it.
- Surreal limitations: It is strange when one has to fiddle with wind and solar power while overunity is so easy to achieve these days.
Luckily MODS can counter these flaws.

8/10, highly recommended.

A text review will not do this game justice, go watch some youtube videos.
In essence you control a squad of crash landed survivors in a semi post apocalyptic landscape. You have to build a base, take care of your squad mentally and physically, and survive the harsh environments and hostile entities. You can pause, slow or fast forward time. You have to manually equip your squad members how you see fit. You can queue commands and order them by priority and basically automate your squad to accomplish tasks. You can capture enemies, tame animals, harvest organs, become cannibals, or become traders. You get to shape your society how you want.

The base building is very deep, for example if you want to make your food supplies last you need to create a room with air conditioning unites to make it freezing temperatures. You need to prepare for winter and have warm clothes for your survivors and heaters. Store enough food to survive the winter because your crops will perish. You can do indoor crops using sun lamps and energy generators. There is just so much. I haven't tried any of the DLC yet so I cannot comment on that.

Go ahead you can! 10/10

This game has been my favourite for six years now, since beta. It has won labour of love award and it deserves it. It has amazing DLCs which truly expand the game and meaningful updates. The modding community simply spectacular and the DLCs interact with each other. The gameplay is endless from full pacifist runs with religious missionaries and allies to cannibalistic monster slavers. On this account, I am nearly at 1000 hours, on my previous account I was around 500. I can easily see myself playing this game for 10k hours without getting bored or running out of gameplay. Truly a masterpiece and there isn't any other game that feels like this. To think the creator started this by himself goes to show passion projects can outperform AAA games.
